author: 5kO0
content:
Implemented (this session). Took the \"or fix Vec<u8> digest to [u8; 32]\" path — the audit's primary concern was the heap allocation per CID, which the inline-array fix addresses without the consumer-wide ripple of swapping to the upstream cid crate.

Code change in proto-blue-lex-data/src/cid.rs:
  Cid::digest:        Vec<u8>  →  [u8; 32]
  Cid::new:           takes [u8; 32] (still pub const fn)
  Cid::for_cbor / for_raw:  Sha256::digest(...).into() — exploits sha2's GenericArray<u8, U32> -> [u8; 32] From impl.
  Cid::for_raw_hash:  takes [u8; 32] directly; the runtime length-check it carried is now an invariant of the type, so the function is infallible (no Result needed).
  Cid::from_bytes:    on parse, validates digest_len == SHA256_DIGEST_LEN and returns InvalidDigestLength otherwise. CAR / firehose / wire-form CIDs that don't match the AT-protocol shape now fail at the parse boundary instead of being constructed as a value.
  Cid::is_dasl_compliant:  no longer needs to check digest length — invariant of the type.

Copy NOT derived — left as Clone-only with an explanatory comment in the struct definition. Adding Copy would trigger clippy::clone_on_copy on hundreds of pre-existing cid.clone() sites across the workspace; that's a separable ergonomic cleanup outside #7's scope (the audit's concern was the heap allocation).

Size impact:
  Before: u8(1) + u64(8) + u64(8) + Vec<u8>(24 bytes ptr+len+cap) = 41 bytes inline + 32 bytes heap
  After:  u8(1) + u64(8) + u64(8) + [u8; 32](32 bytes inline)     = 49 bytes inline, NO heap
  Net: +8 bytes inline, -32 bytes heap, eliminated allocator-pressure-per-Cid, better cache behaviour for Vec<Cid> / BlockMap. CIDs are constructed in dense loops (firehose decode, MST traversal, CAR parsing) so the heap-allocation removal compounds.

Verification (rust-quality §honest reporting):
  cargo build --workspace                                           PASS
  cargo test --workspace                                            PASS (67 suites, 0 failures)
  cargo test -p proto-blue-lex-data                                 PASS (4 unit tests + 1 doctest, including the existing varint-overflow regression)
  cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings             PASS
  cargo fmt --all --check                                           PASS
  cargo +nightly fuzz run car_parse -- -runs=2000                   PASS (no crashes; corpus exercises Cid::from_bytes via CAR block headers)

Behavioural change:
  - Cid::for_raw_hash signature changed from \`fn(Vec<u8>) -> Result<Self>\` to \`const fn([u8; 32]) -> Self\`. Callers passing a Vec<u8> need to convert with try_into or `.as_slice().try_into()` first; the function no longer returns Result. No internal call sites used this — public-API breaking only for downstream consumers.
  - Cid::from_bytes now rejects non-32-byte digests with InvalidDigestLength. Previously it accepted any digest length, which let non-DASL CIDs round-trip through the type. The fuzz target rejects-overflowing-digest-length test still passes (any error variant is acceptable; what's verified is no panic).
  - Cid::digest type changed from Vec<u8> to [u8; 32]. The codebase is the only consumer that touched the field directly (search-confirmed); all other usage went through Cid::for_cbor / Cid::to_bytes / Display etc., which preserve their signatures.

Category: A (root-cause) — the heap allocation is gone at the type level, not just at one site. The 32-byte invariant is enforced by construction; the audit's concern is addressed at the foundation.

Did NOT migrate to the cid crate (the \"or\" half of the issue): that's a separable refactor with a much wider blast radius — would need a separate sub-issue if anyone wants to take it up. The inline-array fix already covers the audit's stated motivation (no heap allocation, stricter type, better cache behaviour).
